# Awesome Jev Papers

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A curated arXiv reading list on **Jev, System One, and typed decision models**: models that return probabilities over supplied options, and the methods, evaluations, and agent applications built around them.

**Updated: 2026-10-16** · **172 papers** · **116** directly related to Jev · **52** related models and methods · **4** foundations · **51** papers with verified author-linked code

Main window: **2025-10-16 through 2026-10-16**, by first submission. Each entry pins the version reviewed for this snapshot. Earlier foundations are listed separately.

Jev means TypeSafe's hosted model. Similar interfaces do not establish reproduction of its proprietary architecture or training. Notes describe the research, not independently reproduced results. Preprints and results from different experimental setups should not be read as a shared performance leaderboard.

**Data and maintenance:** [JSON](data/papers.json) · [BibTeX](references.bib) · [Selection rules](docs/METHODOLOGY.md) · [Search log](docs/SEARCH_LOG.md) · [Screening ledger](data/screening.json) · [Pending](docs/PENDING.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

<a id="recommended-reading"></a>
## Recommended reading

Ten starting points arranged as a reading path across evidence reviews, benchmarks, models, calibration, security, and applications. This is not a performance ranking; all other included papers remain in the catalogue.

- [Typed Decision Models: An Early Evidence Audit and Evaluation Checklist](#paper-2609-32160) — Audits the first wave of Jev and typed-decision research and derives an evaluation checklist.
- [Benchmarking System One decision models against trained classifiers and language models for automated decision gates](#paper-2610-00346) — Compares Jev and other decision models with trained classifiers and generative models under matched decision requests.
- [System1-Arena: Which Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?](#paper-2610-21244) — Introduces matched probability-scored tasks and closed-loop environments to compare fast decisions with reasoning.
- [Jeva: System One Models from First Principles](#paper-2610-18773) — Designs decision-native representations for missing answers, option permutations, candidate scaling and cache reuse.
- [SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents](#paper-2610-05107) — Trains calibrated single-pass search decisions and delegates uncertain judgments to a reasoning and generation system.
- [Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models](#paper-2610-19811) — Studies risk-budgeted threshold selection and conservative fallbacks across moderation, safety and reranking tasks.
- [Evaluating System One Models for Agent Security Decisions: Reliability, Calibration, and Selective Automation](#paper-2609-33401) — Evaluates security accuracy, calibration and allow/block/escalate policies for Jev and peer models.
- [Consider, Then Choose: Order-Invariant Decisions in System One Models](#paper-2610-18233) — Proposes Runoff candidate screening and balanced comparison to reduce option-order dependence across models including Jev.
- [JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs](#paper-2610-21412) — Benchmarks agent decisions and learns trajectory-specific delegation thresholds; trains a model using Jev labels.
- [System One Models for Wireless Decision-Making:Applications and Performance Evaluation](#paper-2610-04345) — Uses Jev in wireless control case studies to measure decision quality and client-observed latency tradeoffs.

<a id="reuse-and-updates"></a>
## Reuse and updates

Full author lists, submission and revision dates, versions, relation notes, and short evidence excerpts are available in [JSON](data/papers.json) and the [evidence ledger](docs/EVIDENCE.md). A code link means an author-linked public repository was reachable, not that its experiments were reproduced.

Edit the data, then run the commands below. GitHub Actions checks catalogue consistency; it does not automatically add papers.

```sh
python scripts/render.py
python scripts/validate.py
```
